name: Sharwa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Sharwa (shar1249) is not in the catalog and Glottolog lists no grammar or phonology for it (5 refs: two wordlists/surveys by Brye 2003/2009, two Barreteau et al. overviews, and Gravina 2012). The single title-works with stress in the title, Gravina 2012 'Vowels, consonants and prosody in two Central Chadic languages' (WOCAL 6 proceedings, Köppe, pp. 7-20; listed by Glottolog as a minimal description), is print-only with no DOI and no open copy anywhere reachable; its 'prosody' is almost certainly the Chadic consonant/vowel palatalization-labialization prosody of Jimi and Sharwa that Gravina's 2014 thesis (same author, same two languages, sec. 6.2) develops while explicitly excluding tone and stress. The Brye 2009 wordlist (held by the project) shows tone marks only. No first-hand Sharwa word-stress statement was read; the best new statement not found. Priority for acquiring Gravina 2012 is medium: it is the only phonological description of Sharwa in print, so worth a library check, but the author's own framing makes a stress statement unlikely. Everything downloaded is under with.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. LOT 375. Utrecht: LOT (Leiden University PhD). Sec. 6.2 'Case Study - Jimi and Sharwa', pp. 134-143; sec. 6.3.4 p. 147.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Sharwa stress or tone. Sec. 6.2 gives the shared Jimi/Sharwa consonant inventory (Tables 38-40), Sharwa's three underlying vowels /a ə ɨ/ with seven surface vowels (6.2.3, Table 41) and the /ɨ/ > /ə/ plural (Table 42); Sharwa data 'Gravina n.d., Sharwa lexicon, database' (p. 147). The thesis states on p. 1 that the reconstruction is 'of the sound system of Proto-Central Chadic (though not including tone or stress)' and in the Section III opener 'No attempt has been made to reconstruct tone or stress.' The only 'stress' hits in the whole text are these two scope statements.

sources.citation: Brye, Edward. 2009. Jimjimen, Gude, Tsuvan, and Sharwa Wordlists. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-008. Dallas: SIL International. 9 pp. (SIL archives 9002).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose on phonology. The Sharwa column (L4, ALCAM 214, pp. 3-9) is a 120-item ALCAM list transcribed with tone diacritics (rendered p. 3, saved as : má 'mouth', hèné 'head', gàná 'tongue', ʔwàká 'breast', ʃíɓʷōtē 'hair' with a macron mid tone); no stress marks anywhere. Text layer is garbled by the legacy SIL IPA font, so the page image was checked.

sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic rapid appraisal (survey of 9-10 Feb 2000, Bourrah subdivision): names, six villages, ALCAM lexicostatistics, multilingualism, vitality, attitudes; sec. 1.4 classification (ALCAM 214, Grimes 1996 Biu-Mandara A.8); sec. 4: SIL/CABTAL/NACALCO had no plans to work on Sharwa. The words stress, accent, tone, prosody, phonology do not occur.
